entry.title: Strive Buys $335 Million in Bitcoin After Investors Pour In $369 Million
entry.summary: The Nasdaq-listed bitcoin holder bought as warrant holders exercised, bringing in $369 million, and it now plans a $630 million sale of 15% preferred stock.

entry.title: Anthropic Gives 5% of Itself to the Public. Musk Answers by Giving Away SpaceX Shares
entry.summary: Anthropic committed 5% of its shares to a public benefit fund, and within hours Elon Musk promised a SpaceX share to every American child.

entry.title: XRP Ledger Repairs Its Lending Protocol Before It Goes Live
entry.summary: XRP developers published a second amendment to repair the ledger’s new uncollateralized lending feature while the original still awaits validator approval.

entry.title: Hackers Are Running Apple's iOS on Android Phones for the First Time
entry.summary: Hobbyists are booting iOS 16 on Xiaomi and Nothing phones and posting the proof. It barely works, but it suggests Apple's software is no longer welded to Apple's hardware.

entry.title: Mastercard Brings Its Fraud-Fighting Tools to Stablecoin Payments
entry.summary: Unveiled at Money20/20, the API-based tool combines payment and blockchain intelligence to flag fraud, scams and sanctions exposure before funds move on-chain.

entry.title: Why Some of America’s Biggest Companies Are Objecting to Tokenized Shares
entry.summary: Nine companies, including Verizon, Broadcom and UnitedHealth, have objected to having their shares traded on the planned OKX-ICE tokenized stock venue.

entry.title: US Orders Civilian Agencies to Rip DeepSeek Out of Government Systems
entry.summary: The Department of Homeland Security told civilian agencies to remove China's DeepSeek and any service built on it, and banned buying more, citing the risk of sensitive data reaching Beijing.

entry.title: JPMorgan's JPM Coin Arrives on Ethereum, Putting Bank Dollars on a Public Blockchain
entry.summary: JPMorgan is rolling out JPM Coin on Ethereum for institutional clients, a token backed by dollars in its accounts that settles in seconds, any day of the week.

entry.title: Abandoned Bitcoin? Wallet Targeted by Noah Doe Lawsuit Moves $33 Million
entry.summary: A Bitcoin address dormant since 2013 moved 411.45 BTC worth about $33.4 million, according to Galaxy Research, and it’s among the wallets named in the “Noah Doe” lawsuit.

entry.title: Bitcoin Tests Key Support as Oil and AI Fears Squeeze Markets
entry.summary: Bitcoin keeps limping back to the same floor while $108 oil and 5% yields weigh on risk assets. The chart shows a coiled spring, not a trend.

entry.title: Tom Lee’s Bitmine Adds $30 Million in Ethereum as Buying Nears Its Finish Line
entry.summary: The purchase lifts Bitmine’s stash to 6.04 million ETH—4.9% of supply and 99% of the way to its “Alchemy of 5%” goal—as chairman Tom Lee framed a market-wide selloff as an attractive entry point.

entry.title: Strategy Buys $22M in Bitcoin, Buys Back $193M of STRC
entry.summary: The Bitcoin treasury firm raised its preferred stock buyback cap to $3 billion and now holds 848,517 BTC, bought at an average of $75,446.

entry.title: Morning Minute: Crypto Rebounds as 'Black Monday' Looms
entry.summary: The original “Black Monday” occurred 39 years ago today. Is history about to repeat itself?

entry.title: ‘Terrifying Precedent’: Dutch Hand US Data From Seized Anti-Fascist Server
entry.summary: Police seized the Autistici/Inventati server under a 1981 treaty after the U.S. designated the Italian activist group “global terrorists.”

entry.title: Sam Altman's World Takes Proof-of-Human IDs to Banks, Citing $40B AI Fraud Risk
entry.summary: Bain Capital, VanEck and Pantera Capital are among design partners for the offering, which also lets users delegate proofs to AI agents.

entry.title: UK Trio Jailed Over Home Invasion in Failed Crypto Theft Attempt
entry.summary: The victim was hit over the head before his teenage sister alerted police, who arrested all three men at the scene in May.

entry.title: Zcash Developer Zakura Proposes Fix to Stop Quantum Computers Linking Shielded Swaps
entry.summary: Zakura says a single published Zcash address could let a future quantum attacker link every payment a wallet has ever received.

entry.title: MapQuest Now Shows Drivers Where Flock Cameras Are Watching
entry.summary: MapQuest’s app now offers an optional map layer that plots known license plate readers from Flock Safety and other vendors, as backlash against the cameras grows.

entry.title: Bitcoin ETFs Shed Nearly $1 Billion in Two Weeks as Uptober Stays Red
entry.summary: Bitcoin ETFs lost a net $228.6 million this week, following a $681.1 million drain the week before and pushing October deep into the red.

entry.title: Banks Hold a Lever Over Stablecoin Adoption, BIS Economists Say
entry.summary: A Bank for International Settlements working paper found that stablecoin growth slows when U.S. banks raise deposit rates, with Circle’s USDC most sensitive.

entry.title: Crypto Super PAC Fairshake Pours Millions More Into Defeating Sherrod Brown
entry.summary: An FEC filing shows the Fairshake affiliate Defend American Jobs disclosed roughly $7 million more in ads against the Ohio Democrat, pushing its total past $46 million—days after the PAC expanded its map to 32 House races.

entry.title: Crypto Firms Launch Quantum Alliance as 6 Million Bitcoin Sit Exposed
entry.summary: The nine-member group, modeled on the Internet Engineering Task Force, aims to set open standards for testing quantum-resistance claims as forecasts place the first practical attack in the late 2020s.

entry.title: Chinese Startup StepFun Launches a Phone Built Around an AI Agent, Not Apps
entry.summary: StepFun's STEPX Neo opened for pre-orders in China on Oct. 13 at 3,999 yuan, with an AI agent built into the operating system instead of bolted on as an app.

entry.title: TokenMaxxing: How to Get the Most Out of Your AI Models
entry.summary: AI companies charge by the token, and most people burn them on jobs a cheap model could do. Here's how to spend less and get better results, from your first prompt to your first agent.

entry.title: Tesla Roadster Rocket Is the Cool 'Flying' Car You Can’t Have
entry.summary: Tesla's new Roadster flips through the air, jumps a row of Teslas and lands on SpaceX thrusters. The Rocket version is invite only, not approved for public roads, and not due until 2028.

entry.title: Hackers Jailbreak iPhone 18 Pro on Stage, and It Survives a Reboot
entry.summary: Calif showed an untethered jailbreak on an iPhone 18 Pro running iOS 27.0.1 at Hexacon in Paris. It survived a reboot, but no tool or bug details are public yet.

entry.title: Circle Plans Push Into 40 Emerging Markets as Stablecoins Go Mainstream, CEO Says
entry.summary: Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire told Reuters the USDC issuer plans to enter about 40 emerging and developing markets, citing rising demand in Southeast Asia, Latin America, Africa and the Middle East.

entry.title: Bitcoin Treasury Giant Strategy Faces Index Removal Under Finalized MSCI Rules
entry.summary: The index provider will classify “non-operating companies” as ineligible starting Nov. 30, targeting firms whose balance sheets are dominated by a single asset.

entry.title: India's Cyber Agency Says AI Agents Read Confidential Business Records Without Authorization
entry.summary: India's CERT-In says AI agents exceeded their assigned tasks in tests and read confidential records on live Indian systems.

entry.title: CFTC Wants to Drop Gemini’s $5M Settlement. A Judge Just Said No
entry.summary: The judge ruled that a shift in the CFTC’s enforcement priorities and misconduct allegations against its enforcement division weren’t enough to reopen a deal Gemini signed weeks before trial.

entry.title: Bitcoin Bounces, But Where Does It Go Next? Here’s What the Charts Say
entry.summary: Technical indicators suggest the bullish trend remains intact, but prediction market traders are sending mix signals.

entry.summary: Police seized guns, silencers and more than 2,000 rounds of ammunition, nearly all of it allegedly stolen from the Canadian military.
